name: Anophthalmia-Heart and Pulmonary Anomalies-Intellectual Disability Syndrome
aliases: Anophthalmia with cardiac and pulmonary defects and intellectual disability
Anophthalmia with congenital heart and lung anomalies and cognitive impairment

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Anophthalmia-Heart and Pulmonary Anomalies-Intellectual Disability Syndrome

criteria.description: Bilateral anophthalmia or severe microphthalmia confirmed by clinical and imaging evaluation
Presence of congenital heart defects such as atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, or pulmonary valve stenosis
Structural pulmonary anomalies including hypoplasia or malformations of the lung parenchyma or vasculature
Developmental delay or intellectual disability confirmed by neuropsychological assessment
Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including midface hypoplasia and broad nasal bridge

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral anophthalmia or severe microphthalmia plus congenital heart and pulmonary anomalies with documented intellectual disability
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and developmental assessments; genetic testing may aid in differential diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Complete absence of ocular tissue confirmed by imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect)
searchTerms: congenital atrial and ventricular septal defects

common.symptomName: Intellectual disability ranging from moderate to severe

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to structural anomalies
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from heart defects
lung artery hypertension due to structural problems
pulmonary high pressure from heart abnormalities

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Orbital MRI or ultrasound confirming absence of ocular structures
Chest CT or X-ray showing pulmonary hypoplasia or malformations
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic testing may exclude other syndromes

redFlags: Bilateral absence of eyes detected at birth
Severe congenital heart defects causing cyanosis or heart failure
Progressive respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
references: Orphanet: Anophthalmia-heart and pulmonary anomalies-intellectual disability syndrome, ORPHA:91129
